messages:
maria: Heads-up: saw NaNs in model output when running paged attention + fused flash variant on bf16. Repro on last nightly with batch scheduling enabled. Logs below.

ajay: Ugh. Do you have profiler traces? Is it happening on cold-start or warm cache?

maria: Cold-start after KV page swap. Quick log snippet: 
```
[step=102] kernel=fused_flash_variant launch
softmax: max=783.45, exp overflow -> NaN
KV page evict: evicted_pages=1
```

sophie: max=783.45 seems wild — suggests a runaway logit. What seq len / request mix?

maria: Seq len ~4096 (paged), we chunk to 512 pages. Happens on mixed batches: some requests warm (cache hit), some cold (page load).

lee: Hypothesis: the batching heuristic mixes cold KV entries with warm ones, fused_flash chooses fast softmax path (fp16 accum) without numerically stable subtraction, and bf16 accumulation saturates.

ajay: Can you rerun with NUMERIC_DEBUG=1 and force the numerically stable softmax? Also capture profiler: `profiler --kernel=fused_flash --trace softmax,kv`

maria: Ran that. Profiler shows LSE variance spike right before NaN. Kernel selected: fused_flash for batch_size=8; single-request falls back to paged_flash. Snippet: 
```
softmax_lse: mean=2.4 var=310.1 spike=780.9 -> NaN at t+0.2s
kernel_path: fused_flash_fast_softmax (fp16 accumulate)
```

runtime-bot: deploy 2026-02-12T08:03:22 - Canary: fused_flash updated (clamp patch pending review)

maria: Quick experiments: forcing fp32 accumulation in softmax removes NaNs but ~1.8x slower. Using stable softmax (subtract max before exp) removes NaNs at ~1.05x slowdown.

sophie: Short-term mitigations: 1) change kernel-selection to avoid fused_flash when batch contains mixed cold/warm KV (or >30% cold), 2) add log-sum-exp subtraction/clamp in fused path. Long-term: add auto-detect on softmax variance to fallback.

lee: I'll open PR for heuristic + clamp: heuristic = avoid fused_flash if cold_kv_ratio > 0.3 OR seq_len > 2048; plus clamp exp inputs to +/-15 in fused kernel. Will include perf benchmark.

ajay: Also add a synthetic regression test (nightly) that mixes cold/warm requests; ticket INF-4123 for tracking.

maria: Thanks — I'll attach the full traces and the reproduction harness to INF-4123.

(emoji reactions: :white_check_mark: :warning:)
